title: Reimagine the Chatticus brand and web experience
description:
## Intent

Create one distinctive Chatticus identity across the public marketing site and the product workspace. Lead with the existing control-first position, make named teammates feel present through Vultus-rendered stateful motion, and establish a reusable visual system that is original rather than derivative of any third-party avatar design.

## Definition of Done

- The marketing site runs as its own Next.js surface at chattic.us and the product workspace runs at hey.chattic.us.
- The public site clearly explains named teammates, the shared user-controlled computer, approvals, skills, routines, and work that can continue while the user is away.
- Vultus provides the renderer and mixed model zoo, with meaningful motion states and original role-specific Lottie models.
- The visual identity, typography, color, layout, and motion system are responsive, accessible, and shared with the workspace.
- No third-party character asset or imitated silhouette is shipped without verified reuse rights and attribution.
- Marketing and workspace tests, lint, builds, visual checks, and reduced-motion behavior pass.
- The work is reviewed and integrated into develop before the epic closes.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Milestone source now unifies the static marketing site at chattic.us with the product workspace at hey.chattic.us. The Vultus renderer/model-zoo integration, original role-specific Lottie models, responsive browser QA, and repository gates are complete locally. No AWS deploy has occurred; review, landing in develop, and the ordered production rollout remain, so the epic stays in progress.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Post-rebase validation against current develop passes: Behave 50 features, 269 scenarios, and 1,661 steps; Pytest 427 passed with eight skipped. The redesigned source and ChatticusMarketingWeb stack remain undeployed, and the work has not landed, so the epic stays in progress.
